titles_corrected: Photo 1 shows 'Waterloo Sunrise' (tan spine, matches title 21), Africa39 and February House (photo 6), Great Prints & Printmakers (photo 4, grey cloth, blind stamp, Abrams-style). Photo 2 title page: English Furniture, Georgian Period, Jourdain and Rose, London: B.T. Batsford Ltd. Photo 5: Pijoan Art in the Middle Ages, University of Knowledge Chicago 1940. Source images are only 800x600 so no spine could be read beyond what the first run got.; Unidentified pink spine and grey cloth spine beside Great Prints at left of the right box remain unnamed.; Second pass: enlarged photo 1 to 3x in the browser. Confirmed: THE GALLERIES BOOK (white spine, top of left box), pink spine is NGA Turner, Everybody Who Was Anybody has a Penguin logo (paperback), CONSTABLE olive hardback at top of right box, Monet at Giverny with Mathews Miller Dunbar on spine, Great Prints & Printmakers spine reads WECHSLER at foot.
unreadable_recheck: Checked all four ways: no larger image variants exist on the server (tried 15 URL patterns, all six photos are 800x600 max), lot description is only '2 BOXES OF ART REFERENCE BOOKS', photo 1 enlarged to 3x and zoomed region by region, photos 2 to 6 viewed full size (they are close-ups of English Furniture title page and plate, Great Prints cover, Pijoan title page, Africa39 and February House). Still unreadable: (1) green gilt-tooled cloth book, left box, between the OIL PAINTING STEP-BY-STEP spine and Leon Underwood, spine begins 'THE ... BOOKS' (2) dark blue small book under Toulouse-Lautrec, left box, text '...MUSEUM' (3) green cloth paperback under Everybody Who Was Anybody, top left of left box (4) grey cloth gilt-ruled book between Great Prints and the pink NGA Turner, right box, small text with 'par' (5) maroon gilt upright book between the boxes (6) orange Penguin paperback and (7) white paperback, right box between Africa39 and Memories of the Future (8) author lines for Velazquez, Toulouse-Lautrec, Picasso (9) publisher lettering on Constable (10) Raphael, tan spine in lower right box under the Degas stack (11) dark jacketed hardback upright at right edge, and (12) large Phaidon folio flat at the bottom of the left box. value_no_firsts: A$80-150 for the lot at most: about 29 cheap paperbacks (sold prices A$2-20 each, most under A$15), no early or signed items found. Current bid $45.
viewing_check: 1) Peanuts Jubilee (item 16): check whether it is a hardback in white dust jacket with Holt, Rinehart and Winston 1975 on the title page; a first printing sold A$160.19 on eBay AU 6 Nov 2026. 2) Topolino: flick through the ~12 issues for low numbers (under ~n.300, 1949-1960s); a 1950s issue is worth more than the whole lot. 3) Read the title of the second Asterix and the 'Mo...' book. Otherwise all cheap.
searches_tried: eBay AU sold (opened, 2026-11-09) for every title; AbeBooks title+author for every title; Invaluable for Topolino libretto and Peanuts paperbacks (no useful sales); Invaluable 'asterix goscinny uderzo hodder' (only an Asterix and Cleopatra original-edition lot, no price shown). LiveAuctioneers and the-saleroom not opened for lot 239 titles because none is pre-1960 or a first of a collectable title.

titles_corrected: All 7 photos opened and enlarged 3x. Photo 1 = the three books with a claret jug and two Sevres-style cobalt and gilt porcelain pieces (teapot and sugar bowl). Photos 2 = porcelain close-up. Photo 3 = Our Mutual Friend title page. Photo 4 = school prize label (Kingswood House School, Epsom, Form IX, Xmas Term 1932, presented to C.C.J. Fage(?)). Photo 5 = David Copperfield title page. Photo 6 = school prize label (Heath School, Horsmonden, Kent, Form IV, July 1914, 'in recognition of loyal and efficient discharge of duty as Captain of the School'). Photo 7 = Tennyson Poems title page and a Jellicoe frontispiece (Guinevere).; There are exactly 3 volumes, no fourth book. Earlier note had the bindings wrong: the PURPLE pebble-grain cloth volume with gilt cartouche on the cover is David Copperfield (cover lettering 'COPPERFIELD / CHARLES DICKENS' legible, right of the claret jug), not the Tennyson. The Tennyson is the red cloth volume with orange spine behind the jug, edges and endpaper red (photo 7 bottom edge). Our Mutual Friend is the brown embossed cloth volume with Dickens medallion on the left.; Our Mutual Friend title page confirmed: 'with illustrations by Marcus Stone', 'A reprint of the edition corrected by the author in 1869, with an introduction, biographical and bibliographical, by Charles Dickens the Younger', Macmillan and Co., Limited, St Martin's Street, London, 1930.; David Copperfield: engraved Phiz-style vignette title page 'David Copperfield by Charles Dickens' and a frontispiece, no publisher or date on the pages shown. Publisher unproven; Macmillan 1920s-30s uniform reprint with the Phiz plates is likely. Purple pebble cloth; no photo of the imprint.; Tennyson title page: 'Poems by Lord Tennyson, with an introduction by Horace G. Groser and six illustrations by John Jellicoe', 'London: The Pilgrim Press, 16 Pilgrim Street, E.C.', no date on the title page. AbeBooks dealers list this title as Andrew Melrose, 1906 (first edition); Melrose was at 16 Pilgrim Street, so the Pilgrim Press imprint copy is the same book under a later or alternative imprint, probably c.1906-1914. The Heath School label dated July 1914 is probably in this red volume (marbled red endpaper), which would date the copy to 1914 or earlier, but I could not prove which book the label sits in.
unreadable_recheck: 0 unreadable. Only unproven point: David Copperfield publisher (imprint page not photographed) and which book holds the Heath School 1914 label.

unreadable_recheck: Photo 1 enlarged and zoomed region by region. Still unreadable: three light-blue/teal cloth volumes with gilt monograms, positions 6-8 from the left in photo 1 (between Twelve Tests and Pompeii; spines show only a small gilt device, no title legible). In the horizontal stack on the right of photo 1, five of six volumes have blank/faded spines (the top tan one, the third grey-tan with red label, the cream fourth, and the bottom two red cloth ones); only 'Captains Courageous' is legible. So 3 + 5 = 8 volumes remain unidentified (the earlier count of 9 included Captains Courageous itself and At the Black Rocks which is now read). Photo 2 shows no more spines.

titles_corrected: Lot title is 'VINTAGE SEWING ITEMS, CARDS & AGATHA CHRISTIE NOVELS'. Photo enlarged and zoomed: four black cloth volumes with red top-edge staining and a red spine label panel, 'AGATHA CHRISTIE / CRIME COLLECTION', three novels per volume. This is the Lansdowne Press / Agatha Christie Ltd (Planet Three) omnibus series (AbeBooks lists the same black-and-red 'Agatha Christie Crime Collection' with 'Published by Lansdowne Press').; Spine labels read at best (blurred at 800x600): vol 1 'Appointment with Death / Endless Night(?) / Sad Cypress'; vol 2 'Three Act Tragedy(?) / Lord Edgware Dies / Murder at ... (illegible)'; vol 3 'The Unexpected Guest?? / The Mysterious Mr Quin?? ...' (illegible); vol 4 'Murder on the Orient Express(?)... / Evil Under the Sun(?) / Why Didn't They Ask Evans(?)'. Only vol 1 and the middle line of vol 2 are reasonably certain.; Non-book items confirmed: Caley's 'Cranford' chocolate tin (lid on the floor in front, full of buttons), Ideal tin (red with horse/trees pattern, sewing reels), card box with playing cards (one with Gainsborough Blue Boy back), oval-mount gilt photo frame with brown mount, cut/pressed glass sauce boat.
unreadable_recheck: Four spines enlarged 4.5x and zoomed. Two of the 12 novel titles are readable with confidence (Appointment with Death, Lord Edgware Dies), the rest only partly. They are ordinary 1980s-90s omnibus reprints, so the exact contents do not change the value.

No auction-house search done: the books are a 1980s-90s omnibus and the rest is general collectables with no auction record likely.

titles_corrected: No.7 corrected: the black box at the top is 'TAHITI: ISLAND OF LOVE / ROBERT LANGDON' lying flat in a black dust jacket. Langdon's book was published by Pacific Publications, Sydney (1959 first, reprints to 1979), not Cassell as the first run guessed (AbeBooks lists Pacific Publications 1972, 1978, 1979 printings only).; No.4: spine reads 'Oasis of the North / Dawn Macleod' in a blue circle, orange cloth, Hutchinson device at foot: confirmed (Hutchinson 1958 first, 1963 and 1966 reprints).; No.5: cream spine reads 'Beautiful Scotland / Painted by E.W. Haslehust R.B.A. / BLACKIE': Blackie's illustrated 'Beautiful Scotland' (Haslehust paintings, text Geddie/Eyre-Todd).; No.6 identified: red cloth spine 'Easy Steps / Men of Might / Vols 1.2' is part of Adelaide Bee Evans's 'Bible Pictures and Stories' set (Easy Steps in the Bible Story, Men of Might, Stories of the Kings, The Children's Friend; Signs Publishing / Pacific Press), two titles bound as Vols 1 and 2. AbeBooks and eBay sell the set of four and single volumes.; No.1: spine reads 'After Dinner Stories by George Robey, Illustrated by H.M. Bateman, Grant Richards' on tan cloth.; No.2: spine reads 'Poetical Works of Adam Lindsay Gordon', dark red cloth, gilt; no publisher on the spine.; No.3: spine reads 'The County Books: Cornwall, Claude Berry, Robert Hale', green cloth.; No.8: 'Gregory's Melbourne Street Directory, 14th Edition 1982-83', white spine with red marker ribbon visible at the foot.; Photo 2 shows a paperback/booklet with a portrait plate captioned 'Lord Fisher' (Admiral Jacky Fisher), open on top of the row; its title is not visible. It is a biography of Lord Fisher of unknown title, probably a mid-century printing (the plate is a halftone on plain paper).; Unidentified spines per photo 1 (left to right): no.11 plain bright-blue cloth, second from left; no.12 pink/peach spine, fifth from left (between Cornwall and Oasis); no.13 dark navy cloth with worn spine and a red ribbon marker, second from right (between Easy Steps and Gregory's); no.10/14 black item lying flat under the row (the black Tahiti dust jacket is the item on top; the base is a black album or box).

value_no_firsts: A$80-170 for the nine readable books together; most are A$5-25 each. Robey A$20-60, Gordon A$8-25 (more if early imprint), Easy Steps/Men of Might A$15-35, Gregory's A$15-25, Beautiful Scotland A$10-25. Unknown blue, pink, navy and black items are the wildcards.
viewing_check: Robey: confirm title page reads Grant Richards and the year (1922 = first); check for the ten Bateman plates. Gordon: read the title page imprint, an 1890s imprint or leather binding is worth more. Open the four blank spines (blue 2nd from left, pink 5th, navy worn 2nd from right, black flat item) and read the Fisher biography's title page. Tahiti: only a 1959 jacketed copy matters.

LiveAuctioneers, the-saleroom, Leski, Leonard Joel, Lawsons, Davidson, ABA and Trove not opened for this lot's titles: none is an early collectable by an Australian auction house standard apart from Gordon and Robey, for which Invaluable and eBay were the available record.

value_no_firsts: Figures: boxed Michonne A$40-67 and boxed Glenn A$50-65 (sold, mostly from US sellers with heavy postage, so Australian-posted prices sit at the low end). Opened pop-up book A$20-34. Total about A$110-165 if the boxes are genuinely sealed or complete. Bid is A$20, estimate A$40-70. Not a flag (no single item reaches A$100).
viewing_check: Look at the box ends and flaps on Michonne and Glenn: factory tape or glue (sealed) and not sun-faded, window plastic undented, no price stickers. Check the Michonne arms and katana are in the tray, Glenn has rifle and knife. Check the pop-up book: every pop-up standing, no torn tabs (an opened copy sells A$20-34, a complete one at the top).
searches_tried: Opened all 5 lot photos full size. eBay AU sold (Michonne, Glenn, pop-up book; results page read, dates, prices and conditions checked 9 Nov 2026), AbeBooks (pop-up book, US$ prices), Invaluable (Michonne: 0 items; pop-up book: 1 irrelevant). LiveAuctioneers not searched for this lot (collector toys sell on eBay). eBay AU sold covers about 90 days only.

titles_corrected: All Men Back, All One Big ... identified from enlarged photo 1 as 'All Men Back - All One Big Mistake' by W.A. (Bill) Bee, Hesperian Press, Perth 1998; Fool's Gold (McGowan) is Lothian 2006 on AbeBooks, not 2004 as first read; Item 22 white spine bottom-left of photo 1 reads 'Michael Brad(y/by)' with a publisher logo and a date range; author not confirmed. Michael F. Braby is the obvious candidate (Butterflies of Australia, CSIRO 2000, 2 vols, see flagged) but NOT confirmed from the photo; Item 21 large butterfly softcover (Cairns birdwing cover) is probably Braby, The Complete Field Guide to Butterflies of Australia (CSIRO 2004/2005) but title not readable in the photo, so priced as a candidate only; Item 12 Colin Burgess Sisters in Captivity is the 2023 Simon & Schuster Australia edition (checked against AbeBooks); Second pass: all 4 photos re-opened and the left-hand spine column of photo 1 enlarged to 10x and 16x. The photos are only 800x600 pixels, so spines in that column are at the resolution limit. Confirmed readable: 'ALL MEN BACK / ALL ONE BIG', 'SANDERS DFC / OUT OF THE DARKNESS' (author prefix 'Frank'), a green spine ending 'NEIL PATON', a dark spine 'the untold story' with an author starting 'Jane G', a magenta cloth spine with two pink bands (title not legible at any zoom), a white spine with small black text ending '...BRADY/BRADY-like' (not legible), blue 'THE ... GLORIOUS YEARS'. Nothing more can be read from the photos.
unreadable_recheck: Second pass at 10x and 16x on photo 1 and re-check of photos 2 to 4. The magenta pink-banded spine, the white spine (author ends '...AEL BRAD..', text too small to tell Brady from Braby), 'The Wizard ...' (black jacket, green cloth, hidden behind Helpmann) and the author of 'the untold story' (Jane G...) cannot be read from 800x600 photos. They were NOT priced. A web search on 'the untold story' with Jane G... surnames gave no unique match; 'The Wizard ...' has too few letters to search. These need a hand at the viewing on Tue 10 Nov.

value_no_firsts: A$150-300 if every piece is sold singly online (Marvel ST A$5-15 each, Gold Key ST A$14-19 each, Orphan from Krypton about A$20, Penny Arcade A$22, Star Trek III magazines A$5-18 each, Simpsons A$3-8 each, Donald Duck digests A$5-15 each, cards A$20-60 for the two bags). A realistic hammer for the box is A$40-90 (estimate A$40-70, current bid A$15). Nothing in the visible stack reaches A$100 on its own.
viewing_check: Read the numbers on the Gold Key tags: 90210-401 to -711 are common (A$12-25), but any Gold Key with a 10210- code or a 12c/15c cover is a 1967-72 issue worth A$20-400 (Gold Key Star Trek #1 asks US$415 VG). Look for a Simpsons Comics #1 and check the Frew Phantom number (a low-number Frew, under about #300, can ask A$100-200). Count the fact cards in the two bags and read the red 'No.5' comic and the yellow-armour item.

value_no_firsts: Nearly all 34 searched titles are cheap (A$5-25 each, remainder/art reference). Box value about A$80-150 for the two boxes unless the Vettriano is signed (A$60-200 alone) or Eton Days first edition (A$35-55) and Faber Gallery booklets (A$15-25 each, about A$24 each in a lot of 5, A$120 for the lot) are in good order. Estimate 40-70, current bid A$15.
viewing_check: 1) Open the Jack Vettriano Lovers & Other Strangers (Pavilion, black spine with A logo) and check the title page for a signature; also the printing line (signed first A$203 sold 8 Nov 2026, unsigned A$6-16). 2) Check the Eton Days (Lund Humphries 1976, A$55 sold) copy and jacket. 3) Look at the thin booklets (Goya, Kandinsky, Cezanne, Augustus John, Giovanni ...): if Faber Gallery they are about A$15-25 each. 4) Read the spines of the 9 unread books (Hornsby ART &, green linen book, black crest-logo hardback, three cream hardbacks) and the Hughes and Johnson book. 5) I Shed My Skin (Forty South 2020) retails A$75 new, check for Giblin or Hay signature.
searches_tried: AbeBooks (opened every title, sorted by price, links recorded), eBay AU sold (opened every title with 10 s gaps, no bot check), Invaluable search (opened for most titles, mostly 0 items; opened two lots whose sold price is hidden behind subscription), Forty South shop page for Giblin. LiveAuctioneers, the-saleroom, Leski, Lawsons not opened (not relevant to these mass-market art books). Google search used only to identify Giblin book.

entries.item: The Animals Noah Forgot (Paterson/Lindsay), Box C
entries.why: Cannot tell the 1933 Endeavour Press first from the 1971/1979 Ure Smith reprints from the photo.
entries.value: 1933 first with jacket sold A$220 (Invaluable, 23 Nov 2022); plain first asks about A$49; reprints sell A$10-35 (eBay AU Oct 2026).
entries.check: Title page: Endeavour Press 1933? Dust jacket present? Ure Smith means reprint.

entries.why: MUP 1957 first asks about A$79; Hale & Iremonger reprint about A$7.
Single ask about A$55, no sold record.

value_no_firsts: No true firsts of value. Baldacci run: 18 Pan paperbacks at A$5-9 each sold (about A$115 as singles, plus about 8 unread paperbacks). Australian titles mostly A$5-35 each. Realistic box value is low (A$60-150 hammer territory); the single upside is The Animals Noah Forgot if it is the 1933 Endeavour first.
viewing_check: Animals Noah Forgot title page and jacket (Endeavour Press 1933 vs Ure Smith).; Melbourne Scene imprint (MUP 1957).; Flip the 8 loose Baldacci paperbacks and check for signed copies or hardbacks.; Read the thin books beside Taim Bilong Masta and A Separate Creation, the two polka-dot volumes, and the unmatched Calder, Across the Top, Urban Wildlife and Peaceful Australia.; Check Victor Harbor for Ainslie Roberts limited edition.; Check Pizzey Separate Creation for a signature.

Some multi-quantity eBay items show 'out of stock' rather than 'sold on' but still show the price.
